approach:
Root cause: after a squash the host's commit is not a descendant of the job's landed commit, and `resync_tip` (crates/athena-core/src/land.rs:218) repairs that with `git.replay`, which rebuilds every later commit under new ids. The branch leaves its remote copy's history, so a plain push is refused. The drain never pushes.

Change, in the order the code runs:
1. `resync_tip` builds a merge commit instead of replaying. It takes `git.merge_tree(landed, head, merged)` for the tree and `git.commit_tree(tree, [head, merged], message, sign)` for the commit. The first parent is the branch head, so every old commit stays an ancestor. The message has no marker line and no `Athena-` trailer. The no-op cases are kept (merged already an ancestor of head; landed not on head). A merge conflict is an error and nothing moves. `Athena::resync_onto_merge` moves the branch with the existing `reset_keep`.
2. A shared gate rule, `invariant::merge_paths_not_taken(git, tree, parents)`. It returns the paths where `tree` differs from the first parent and equals no other parent's content. `classify_pre_merge` (invariant.rs:320) gets a new first rule: a merge with no such paths adds nothing a parent does not already hold, so it is `RecordsOnly`. `resync_tip` calls the same function on the tree it built, before committing. If any path is not taken verbatim from a parent (main and the branch both changed one file since the landing), it errors naming the paths and moves nothing. So every merge it makes passes the history check, `classify_commit` and `check_pr_head`, with no message marker.
3. Already-landed commits stay in the append-only branch. `GitLandingRecords::commits` (gh/records.rs:128) leaves them out using the landing records: each `head_sha` whose `host_commit` is an ancestor of `expected_base` is passed as `^head_sha` to a new `land::pr_commits_excluding`. `pr_commits` is unchanged for callers without records. No message is read.
4. `Athena::push_working_branch(ui) -> bool` in land.rs does a plain push of the current branch to `origin` through `GitRemote::remote_head` and `GitRemote::push` (no force option, gh/remote.rs:10). A remote already holding head is silent. No `origin`, detached HEAD or no commit is a silent skip. A failed ls-remote or push prints `warning: could not push <branch> to origin: <reason>; the landing stands` and returns false; it never returns an error. `after_merge` (gh/landing.rs:959) calls it after the resync, which covers `athena land --pr` and the drain's `PrLander` (both go through `Athena::land_pr`, landing.rs:952).
5. Drain: `Steps` gets a defaulted `fn push_after_landing(&self) {}` (same pattern as `config_after_landing`, drain.rs:583). `Drain::land` (drain.rs:1785) calls it right after a `Landing::Landed` is recorded, under the landing lock that serial and concurrent drains share. `RealSteps` overrides it with `self.athena.push_working_branch(self.ui)`; after `after_merge` already pushed, it is a silent no-op, so the real drain pushes once. The in-crate `Stub` records the call, so the drain test sees the push without push logic in a double.
6. Two fixtures that resync a checkout that is main itself (test_support.rs:559, trailer_stop.rs:131) use `reset_keep` instead, since attribution walks main's first-parent line from C0.

Revision answers. Findings 1 and 2: criterion 6 now sets fails_without and a seam (below). Findings 3 to 6 (files outside the reading's list): each stays, because the listed files cannot carry the change. invariant.rs and landing_tests.rs hold the rule that keeps CI's history check (history.rs:142-153, which classifies every commit in merge_base..tip) from failing on a resync merge that carries main's other governed content. records.rs is where landing records pick a pull request's commits, and without the exclusion throughput.rs:397 counts landed jobs twice. after_merge_tests.rs line 103 asserts the old text `rebuilt on the merged commit` and must follow the new message. The scope question goes to the user in open_questions. Also fixed from the last plan: the criterion 8 diff command had a path typo, and the demonstration step references now match the steps below.

Refusal corpus: no reading, plan or request parser changes, so `refusal_corpus` is not touched. The gate rule's input forms are in the commit-shape table below.

Commit-shape table (pre-merge classification, `classify_pre_merge`, used by `pr_commits`, `check_pr_head` and the history check):
| Shape | Outcome after the change |
|---|---|
| Job landing commit (adds one job's closing records, verification in tree) | JobLanding (unchanged) |
| Records-only commit | RecordsOnly (unchanged) |
| Owner-path commit | RecordsOnly where the rules exclude the path, else GovernedChange (unchanged) |
| Intervention commit | DeclaredIntervention (unchanged) |
| Retry-after-block landing (a later commit adds outcome-landed.json) | JobLanding (unchanged) |
| Resync merge, main moved only by the squash (tree equals first parent) | RecordsOnly (new rule; before, rule 4) |
| Resync merge, main also carries other governed content, verbatim from the second parent | RecordsOnly (new; before, GovernedChange) |
| Merge with a path matching no parent (auto-merged blob, hand-written content) | falls through to the old rules: GovernedChange unless it closes a job or declares an intervention (unchanged); resync_tip refuses to build it |
| Merge whose second parent is an unlanded branch | RecordsOnly only for paths taken verbatim; that branch's own commits are in the range and judged one by one |
| Commit already named by a landing record whose host commit is on the base | dropped from landing intents and landing records by the record-based exclusion; still seen by check_pr_head and the history check, where it passes as the job landing it is |

decisions.choice: Build the merge tree with merge_tree(base = landed, ours = head, theirs = merged), commit it with commit_tree(parents head then merged), and move the branch with the existing reset_keep.
decisions.reason: A plain git merge uses the real merge base and conflicts whenever a later job edits the landed job's lines. With the landed commit as base only main's changes beyond the landed job come in. The helpers exist, keep local edits, and follow signs_commits.

rejected.option: git merge in the work tree
rejected.why: It conflicts on later edits of landed lines, can leave a half-done merge, and bypasses the signing and keep-edits behavior.

rejected.option: Keep replay and force-push or push_if_remote_at
rejected.why: Out of scope and rejected by the request; it treats the symptom.

decisions.choice: Make the history gate accept a merge by content: every path where the merge differs from its first parent must equal some other parent's content. One shared function in athena-gate, used by classify_pre_merge and by resync_tip before it commits.
decisions.reason: check_after_cutover (history.rs:142-153) classifies every commit in merge_base..tip, and CI runs it on pull requests, so a resync merge carrying other governed content would fail every later pull request. Content taken verbatim from a parent is either on main (attribution covers it) or in the range (each commit is judged on its own). It needs no landed sha, no message and no extra argument, and the same function limits what resync_tip may create so the two cannot disagree.

rejected.option: Skip any merge whose other parent is on main
rejected.why: An arbitrary tree could ride a merge.

rejected.option: Require the tree to equal merge_tree(landed, p1, p2) in the gate
rejected.why: The gate would need the landed sha, which only a message or record can supply.
It can fail CI permanently for a merge carrying other governed content.

decisions.choice: Exclude already-landed commits from landing intents and landing records using the landing records (head_sha of each landing whose host_commit is an ancestor of the base), with no message marker.
decisions.reason: The repository's rule is that messages are never read (land.rs:245-246, invariant.rs:311). Landing records already hold head_sha and host_commit (athena-data/src/history.rs:228-231). The landing head carries every commit the squash held, so ^head_sha is exact and a forged message hides nothing. Without it throughput.rs:397 would count a landed job's commits again.

rejected.option: A marker line in the merge message, checked against the tree
rejected.why: Free text deciding what is judged.
Double counts JobLanding commits and intents name old jobs.

decisions.choice: Do not change check_pr_head or the history check's range; state the growth in the CHANGELOG and risks.
decisions.reason: Under append-only, origin/main..head grows by every landing. Each old landing commit still classifies as the valid job landing it is and the resync merges classify as RecordsOnly, so the checks pass, but they walk more commits. Excluding landed heads there needs records access in pr_check.rs and history.rs, which widens scope further. Per-job branches (D167) are the long-term answer.

rejected.option: Exclude landed heads in history.rs and pr_check.rs too
rejected.why: More scope in files outside the request; can follow once the cost shows.

decisions.choice: Push from two places through one helper: after_merge (for athena land --pr and PrLander) and a defaulted Steps::push_after_landing called by Drain::land (for the drain).
decisions.reason: Drain tests use Steps doubles that never reach after_merge, and config_after_landing shows the pattern. The land --pr command needs the real gh, so only after_merge can be tested. The helper does nothing when the remote already holds head, so the real drain pushes once.

rejected.why: No drain test could see it without push logic in a double.

rejected.option: Push only in commands::land and RealSteps::land
rejected.why: commands::land needs the real gh; no test could show it.
Every Steps double in drain.rs, tests/drain.rs, job_plan.rs and focus.rs would change.

decisions.choice: A failed or refused push is a warning line; no origin is a silent skip; the push is GitRemote::push, never forced.
decisions.reason: The merge is already done on the host, so a refused push must not undo it or trigger a drain retry. Many drain fixtures have no origin and would otherwise warn on every landing.

rejected.option: Return the push error from after_merge or the drain
rejected.why: It turns a finished landing into a failure.

decisions.choice: Move the two fixtures that resync a checkout that is main itself (test_support.rs:559, trailer_stop.rs:131) to reset_keep.
decisions.reason: Attribution walks main's first-parent line from C0 (attribution.rs:386-409); a merge on a branch named main would put C0 off it. Nothing followed the landed commit there, so the old replay result equals reset_keep. Merge-shape coverage is in the new tests.

rejected.why: athena check --attribution on the fixture would report the cutover commit off main's first-parent line.

decisions.choice: Leave Git::replay and athena-git/src/lib.rs untouched; gh/mod.rs needs no change either.
decisions.reason: replay stays public with its own tests, so no dead-code warning; removing it is a separate clean-up. No new module is added, and merge_tree, commit_tree, reset_keep, push_branch and diff_tree already exist.

decisions.choice: Keep the four files outside the reading's list (invariant.rs, landing_tests.rs, records.rs, after_merge_tests.rs) and put the scope decision to the user.
decisions.reason: Without them a resync merge can fail CI's history check, landed jobs are counted twice, or an existing test fails on the new message text. The first two are a correctness need, not a convenience.

risks.risk: Append-only growth: squashed landing commits never become reachable from main, so every later head's own-commit range grows by each landing, and the CI history check (history.rs:143-153) and check_pr_head classify all of them each run.
risks.mitigation: Each old landing commit is a valid job landing and each resync merge is records only, so the checks pass. Landing intents and records stay short through the record-based exclusion. The cost is a few git calls per commit; a follow-up can apply the same exclusion in history.rs and pr_check.rs. The CHANGELOG entry states the growth; per-job branches (D167) are the long-term answer.

risks.risk: resync_tip is stricter than the replay: a file changed on both sides since the landing is an error even when git could auto-merge the hunks, because the merged blob would match neither parent.
risks.mitigation: The error names the paths and the branch is unchanged, as for a conflict, and the maintainer merges by hand. The common case (main moved only by the squash) gives a tree equal to the head's. Test (d) of criterion 4 covers it.

risks.risk: The verbatim-from-a-parent rule is looser than a landing: a hand merge can bring in another unreviewed branch's content.
risks.mitigation: That branch's own commits are in the range or on main and are judged one by one; the merge adds only paths equal to a parent's. A path with new content still fails as GovernedChange. A gate test covers it.

risks.risk: The push is refused or origin is unreachable; the first landing after this change may be refused once because the remote copy was force-pushed by hand earlier.
risks.mitigation: A warning line gives the reason, the landing and local resync stand, and the next landing pushes the whole append-only history with a plain push after the maintainer reconciles the remote once.

risks.risk: A failed ls-remote or push inside the drain's landing lock could wait on a slow network.
risks.mitigation: One git call per landing, with the same network exposure as the landing's own pushes; it holds no records or job state, and a failure is only a warning.

demonstrations.method: A land.rs unit test on real git with a real bare repository. Build the existing landing scenario on a branch (job A landed, later job B, a hand edit). Make a bare repo with `git init --bare` in a tempdir, add it as `origin` and push the branch, so the remote copy holds the previous head. Build the host squash as the existing resync test does (tree of the landed commit, parent the base). Call resync_tip and move the branch to the result with reset_keep. In the same test, contrast: `git.replay(squash, landed, head)` is not a descendant of the previous remote head and push_branch of it errors.
demonstrations.observes: is_ancestor(previous remote head, tip) and is_ancestor(squash, tip) are both true, git.push_branch("origin", branch, &tip) succeeds, and the bare repository's branch equals tip.
demonstrations.fails_without: With the replay-based resync_tip the tip is not a descendant of the previous remote head, so the first assertion fails and the plain push is refused.

Nothing is faked; real git.

demonstrations.method: land.rs unit tests on real repositories: (a) merged already an ancestor of head returns None; (b) landed not on head returns None; (c) job B edits the same line job A landed and the squash differs on that line, so merge_tree conflicts: resync_tip errors and head is unchanged; (d) both sides change one file in different hunks, so merge_tree auto-merges a blob that matches neither parent: resync_tip errors naming the path, head unchanged (via the shared gate function). Then Athena::resync_onto_merge on case (c) returns an error saying the branch is unchanged and athena.head() is the same.
demonstrations.observes: None for (a) and (b); errors for (c) (message contains `conflict`) and (d) (message names the path); head is the same sha before and after; resync_onto_merge's error text says the branch is unchanged.
demonstrations.fails_without: A resync that moved the branch on conflict, or kept an auto-merged blob the gate would refuse, would change head or return Ok, so the assertions fail.

demonstrations.method: gh/tests.rs test `after_a_merge_the_working_branch_is_pushed`. Use set_up()'s Athena (as after_merge_tests.rs does), add a bare `origin` and push the branch, land a commit with the `land` helper, build the host squash as the existing after_merge test does, and call Athena::after_merge with a Landed report. Second test: a report that is not Landed pushes nothing and logs nothing. Third: origin set to a missing path gives a `warning:` line and after_merge still returns Ok. Plus `landing_records_leave_out_landed_commits`: with one landing recorded for job A, the next GitLandingRecords intent and landing list only job B.
demonstrations.observes: The bare repository's branch equals athena.head() after after_merge (a descendant of the earlier remote head); the Lines log has a `pushed` line after the `merged` line. A not-landed report leaves the bare branch where it was. A missing origin gives a warning and Ok. (Also run `cargo test -p athena-core landing_records_leave_out_landed`: the second landing's intent names only job B.)
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the push call in after_merge the bare branch stays at the earlier head and the equality fails. Without the record-based exclusion the second intent also names job A.

open_questions: User: May this job widen beyond the nine listed deliverables to crates/athena-gate/src/invariant.rs, crates/athena-gate/src/landing_tests.rs, crates/athena-core/src/gh/records.rs and crates/athena-core/src/gh/after_merge_tests.rs? The first two keep a resync merge that carries main's other governed content from failing CI's history check; records.rs stops landed jobs being listed (and counted) again; after_merge_tests.rs asserts the old message text.

User: Is the working branch ever `main` itself? If so, the host's linear-history and pull-request rules will refuse the plain push of a merge commit (shown as a warning), and a local `athena check --attribution` would report the cutover commit off main's first-parent line. The plan assumes a separate working branch.
User: Should a follow-up update docs/design/native-pr-landing.md §5.2a and add a decision-log entry superseding D88's replay tradeoff? The plan leaves them out as outside the request's file list.
Host: Do the remote's branch rules on the working branch's copy allow merge commits and non-linear history? The plan cannot read them; a refusal appears as a warning and the landing stands.

User: Under append-only the pull-request range (origin/main..head) grows by every landing, so the CI history check and check_pr_head classify more commits each time. Is that acceptable until per-job branches (D167) land, or should a follow-up exclude landed heads in history.rs and pr_check.rs too?
